findings.summary: Adolf Martens (1850–1914) was a German metallurgist honored as the namesake of martensite, a hard microstructure formed via a diffusionless solid-state phase transition. He also conducted early experimental work on the relationship between friction, sliding speed, and viscosity, contributing to the foundational understanding later formalized as the Stribeck curve. His career spanned materials science and tribology at the intersection of engineering and physics.

mechanisms.title: Martensitic transformation
mechanisms.explanation: A diffusionless, solid-state phase transition in which carbon-rich phases in steel undergo a rapid, coordinated lattice change, producing a hard, brittle microstructure named in Martens' honor.

mechanisms.title: Friction and viscosity experimentation
mechanisms.explanation: Early experimental exploration of the functional relationship between coefficient of friction, sliding speed, and viscosity, predating and contributing to the later Stribeck curve formulation.

unknowns: The precise internal physical mechanism driving the diffusionless lattice change in martensite formation
